The problem can also bee seen in the sample [plnkr](https://angular.io/resources/live-examples/router/ts/plnkr.html) of the [router and navigation develorper guide](https://angular.io/docs/ts/latest/guide/router.html) on the angular website.
Steps:
-  pop out the preview window to see the address bar
-  click on a crisis and edit the text
-  use the browser back commands to go back. 

The url changes even if the user clicks cancel on the popup

Can confirm that using `Location.back()` changes the URL as well, not just the browser buttons. I have a modal where the user selects to stay on the page or go back - the component stays active, but the URL changes, and subsequent presses on the return button change the URL further back. This also happens if one uses `window.history.back()`
+1, I confirm location.back() changes the URL on final version 2.0.0. Any news about a future fix ?

I can confirm this problem too and want to highlight another problem related to this one.

Pressing the browsers back-button will also trigger `window.history.back()` even if the guard returns _false_, so if the user continues to navigate in a forward direction but then decides to go back and presses the browsers back-button he will navigate too far back.

For example: 

```
VIEW_1 -- navigate to --> VIEW_2
(backButton) --> guard returns false       //still triggers window.history.back()
VIEW_2 -- navigate to --> VIEW_3
(backButton) --> results in Navigation to VIEW_1
```

@strpipe This will also appen in this case

```
VIEW_1 -- navigate to --> VIEW_2
VIEW_2 -- navigate to --> VIEW_3
(backButton) --> guard returns false
User does something to correct the guard fail
(backButton) --> guard returns true --> Navigation to VIEW_1
```

Since the `window.history.back()` is always called when finally the guard returns true it will navigate to a page that depends on the number of times the `window.history.back()` was called.

**Current behavior**
This is leftover from : https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/10321

With the following routes:

    path: 'view',
    children: [
        {

            path: ':id',
            component: CustomerViewComponent,
            resolve: {
                customerViewData: CustomerResolve,
            },
            canDeactivate: [CanDeactivateGuard],
            children: [
                {
                    path: 'edit',
                },
                {
                    path: ''
                }
            ]
        }
    ]

If you navigate to a route like this using `skipLocationChange`:

    this.router.navigate(['edit'], { relativeTo: this.route, skipLocationChange: true });

**Expected behavior**

issue.title: Returning `false` on CanDeactivate implementation should not influence browser history

labels.name: needs reproduction
labels.description: This issue needs a reproduction in order for the team to investigate further

issue.body:
**I'm submitting a ...**
```
[x] bug report
[ ] feature request
[ ] support request
```

**Current behavior**
Returning `false` on CanDeactivate implementation influences browser history.
Seems to be leftover from #10321 and #12825

**Expected behavior**
Returning `false` on CanDeactivate implementation does not influence browser history.

**Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions**
Present in Angular Routing Demo plnkr:
https://angular.io/resources/live-examples/router/ts/eplnkr.html

*STEPS TO REPRODUCE*:

1. Click "Crisis Center"
2. Click Crisis Center 1, then 2, then 3
3. Edit Crisis Center 3's "Name" in its details
4. Press browser "Back" button, and press "Cancel" when confirm dialog pops up asking if you want to discard changes
5. Press browser "Back" button again, but this time press "OK" when confirm dialog pops up asking if you want to discard changes
6. *RESULT:*
You are taken back to Crisis Center 1 detail view instead of Crisis Center 2. If you press browser "Forward" button twice, you'll notice that both times you are taken to Crisis Center 3 detail view. The Crisis Center 3 detail view has essentially replaced the Crisis Center 2 detail view history entry.

**What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior?**
I press my browser's "Back" button but then choose to cancel navigation in order to first save pending changes. When I press my browser's "Back" button again, I should navigate to the previous page as if this was the first time I pressed my browser's "Back" button. 

**Please tell us about your environment:**
-Angular demo plnkr (also present in my own ng-cli v1.0.0.24-beta environment)
-Windows 10 x64

* **Angular version:** 2.4.1, Router 3.4.1

* **Browser:** Chrome v55.0.2883.87 m (64-bit) (untested on others)
 
* **Language:** TypeScript 2.0.10
